rationale: C08 plausibly supplied material drafting machinery for the child. It addresses the identical subject of placing Department-related positions in General Schedule grades 16, 17, and 18 and establishes Civil Service Commission control, including special treatment for placement in and removal from grade 18. The child adapts that machinery to a new statutory delegation to the Secretary of Defense and modifies the required Commission approvals. C23 is also strong because it delegates the President's grade-18 placement and removal authority to the Civil Service Commission Chairman without further presidential action, but it does not cover grades 16 and 17 or the same broader procedure. C03 shares the Secretary-of-Defense delegation and no-presidential-action formulation, but concerns unrelated functions and is less concrete as a template.

shared_material.child_excerpt: to authorize positions in the Department of Defense to be placed temporarily in grades 16, 17, and 18 of the General Schedule of the Classification Act of 1949
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Each requested position shall be placed in the appropriate grade of the General Schedule in accordance with the standards and procedures of the Classification Act of 1949
shared_material.explanation: Both establish operative machinery for classifying positions in the top three General Schedule grades under delegated presidential authority.

shared_material.child_excerpt: no position shall be placed in grade 16 or grade 17 pursuant to such authority without the prior approval of the Civil Service Commission
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Each officer or agency ... shall submit to the Chairman of the United States Civil Service Commission such requests for classification of positions in grades 16, 17, and 18 of the General Schedule as may be necessary
shared_material.explanation: The child adapts C08's Commission-centered review mechanism into an express prior-approval requirement for grades 16 and 17.

shared_material.child_excerpt: no position shall be placed in, or removed from, grade 18 ... without the prior recommendation of the Civil Service Commission and approval of the Chairman of the Civil Service Commission
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the placement of positions in Grade 18 of the General Schedule, and the removal of positions therefrom, shall be accomplished by the Chairman of the United States Civil Service Commission (instead of by the President upon the recommendation of the said Commission)
shared_material.explanation: This is a distinctive substantive parallel: both separately regulate placement in and removal from grade 18 through the Commission and its Chairman, displacing direct presidential action.
